institutionName: Institut d'études politiques de Paris (Sciences Po)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I had already lived and worked in Paris before starting my studies at KU, so the exchange semester seemed like a perfect way to go back and reconnect with old friends and once again live in Paris.

Another motivation was the academic opportunities. Sciences Po Paris is a highly renowned school with really good education. I had heard many good things about the place from friends in Paris before applying. And I was definitely not disappointed!

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Finding information on host universities websites can be very difficult in general. I do however think that the Sciences Po website is quite straightforward. There is a section about exchange programme where most information was available. The course catalogue is also available on the website in good time so you can look at classes before actually deciding to apply (there can be changes in the catalogue though, so you cannot be a hundred percent sure that a specific course will be offered in the final catalogue).

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a Zoom meeting set up with an academic adviser in charge of the exchange programme when I arrived in Paris where we got pretty much all the information we needed and contact information on who to get in touch with if we had any issues. When the semester started we could pick up our student ID card in a tent set up in the rue saint-Guillaume garden (remember to finish your administrative registration on the student platform in due time!).

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I did not receive so much assistance, but I am sure it was available if I had needed it.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Finding accommodation in Paris can be really difficult, stressful and expensive. I recommend joining different facebook groups for housing in Paris. They seem very chaotic, but they do work. I have found housing in there multiple times in Paris. But be careful, a lot of people are trying to scam. Use your common sense and definitely do not send any money before you have visited the appartement/room. Another option is using websites like la carte des colocs if you want to live with roommates. Sciences Po also have a website with housing offers, but it seemed like most were for people staying in Paris for 1 year or more.

For this exchange stay I lived with another Danish student who was also doing an exchange semester. She had found the flat via the facebook group for Danish people living in Paris “Padam padam”. I really recommend joining that one, it is less chaotic and there are less scammers.

In general, it is hard to find housing in good time in Paris when it is for short-term stays. It is not uncommon that flats/rooms are posted just few weeks (or even days) before move-in. I also met some students who had not found housing before arriving and started out living at a hostel or Airbnb. Try not to stress too much even if you feel like the start of the semester is rapidly approaching. You will find something eventually!

If you want to be in better time and avoid some of the stress in looking for a place to live you can try to apply for the Cité Universitaire or some of the Sciences Po partnership organizations (Crous e.g.). The Cité Universitaire is located quite far from the city centre and student housing options often have a lot of strict rules, from what I have heard. That is why I preferred finding something on my own, but it is of course a question of personal preference.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
It is not that uncommon to have rentals without contracts in Paris, especially for short-term stays. I have rented without contract two times and there has not been any problems. But be careful of course. Use your common sense and try to avoid landlords that seem sketchy.

Do not be afraid to live in the 19th and 20th arrondissements even if you hear people talking about them being “sketchy” or “unsafe”. They are so nice and they have changed a lot during the last decade.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: As I did not live in student housing I don't know if I am satisfied with it.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The course registration is quite straightforward, but you have to prepare for it in advance. The registration takes place on a first-come-first basis so you have to be ready when it opens. Prepare a prioritized list of courses and alternatives for each course. Remember to verify that they do not have conflicting time schedules.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There are written guides on the Sciences Po website as well as videos guiding you through the registration process. You can also find videos on youtube. Watch these in advance to prepare yourself.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted, except for one that was not offered in the final catalogue.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Watch the video material on the Sciences Po website. Prepare a prioritized list of courses and alternatives. Especially if you have specific courses that are important to you.

Do not hesitate to write professors if you have questions about the content of courses or about pre-requisites.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very interesting courses taught by passionate professors!

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The academic level was, in my opinion, not that high compared to what I am used to at KU. But the courses are livelier and more intensive. There are a lot of presentations/exposés that you have to prepare throughout the semester as well as smaller assignments that you hand in. There are fewer and less heavy readings, but the workload is still higher because you have to prepare a lot of things during the semester.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style is quite different from KU. The classes are often much smaller and much more active participation is expected from the student. In many classes participation is a part of the grade. I had to get used to this style of teaching at first, but I ended up really liking it. The classes become more dynamic and livelier. There are more in-class discussions, and you get a closer relation to your professor and to your fellow students. As there are not too many readings, you have more time to discuss them in-depth in class. Because the assessment take place through-out the entire semester (presentations, assignments, mid-terms, participation etc.) you are not as stressed out in the final exam period.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Behavioral Game Theory (DECO 25A02)
European integration and its challenges: the euro, migration and populism (DSPO 25A02)
Economic Sociology (DSOC 25A01)
Big Data et sciences sociales (CSOC 25F06)
Espace Mondial (ASPO 25F00)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Big Data et sciences sociales was amazingly interesting. I deeply recommend the course if you are interested in quantitative methods in social science. The course is interdisciplinary (it draws on Sociology, Economics, History and Philosophy of Science) and it is taught by two young professors who are really passionate about the course. The atmosphere was really nice and relaxed and the course was filled with interesting discussions. It is taught in French, but you can write exams and participate orally in English if you would like.

The EU course was also very good. The workload was quite big, but I learned so much.

Espace Mondial (international relations, international economy and political sociology etc.) was also very interesting. The class is divided into a main lecture (in French) and smaller class sessions that you can take in English.

All of the courses I took were really good! The professors were highly engaged and there was a very nice atmosphere in the classroom.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Covid-tests are not free if you do not have a carte vitale (French health insurance card). Antigen tests cost 25€ and can be taken at pharmacies.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I bought a subscription for the city bike system (Vélib) which was really cheap. Only 2,9€ per month (although you have to commit to a full year). I would recommend this.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not really participate in things like these.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I am not really sure as I did not really participate. I know that some other exchange students went to social activities such as guided city tours, Erasmus parties and social events etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Go out and meet new people, talk to strangers at cafés and bars and enjoy parisian joie de vivre. Try to learn French - life in Paris is so much more interesting if you speak French, even if it is just a little. 

Sciences Po is very intensive and school can easily take up a lot of your time – remember to enjoy life in Paris as well while you are there!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Visit all the different neighborhoods in Paris. They are all so different. Go to cafés and to restaurants to eat out a lot. It is generally a lot cheaper than in Copenhagen. 

If you climb, go to Fontainebleau or Viaduc des Fauvettes just outside of Paris!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, because I had already lived in Paris before. But also because the culture is not that different from in Denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Take a Lecture course (10 ECTS) instead of only seminar courses (5 ECTS) – local Sciences Po students are required to have Lecture courses. Do not be afraid to take classes in the evening. I had three courses taking place from 19.15 to 21.15. This was a nice occasion to go out to eat or have a drink after class with my classmates.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: French bureaucracy can be a bit much and some administrative processes can seem impossible or paradoxical. But from my experience the system often turns out quite flexible when you actually talk to people. Call or write people at Sciences Po if you have any issues. I could not for example get results from my French test in due time to document my French level, but I was able to take courses in French anyway after I talked to them.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The culture of going to cafés more often and eating out at restaurants a lot. Going out in the evening for a glass of wine. I enjoyed this so much.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1.	Prepare yourself for course registration day. Have a list of courses ready, make a plan. Especially if you have courses that you really want to take.

2.	Do not let the search for housing stress you out too much. Keep your cool, you will find something!

3.	Remember to enjoy your stay and do not stress too much over school, even though the workload can be quite heavy. Try to learn some French, make new friends, and enjoy life in Paris!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Check if you have insurance via Sciences Po (civil liability etc.). I bought a travelers insurance but found out afterwards that I was actually covered by Sciences Po.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
I made new friends from Paris and from all over the world. I had amazingly interesting courses and learned so much. I also improved my French a lot which was important to me. 

In general I just had an amazing time here. I would really recommend going to Sciences Po Paris for an exchange semester (and just going on an exchange stay in general).

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: There was water leaking from the ceiling in my apartment when I arrived, but luckily it got fixed pretty quickly. Covid was also a bit challenging, as we had to wear face masks inside the school. Otherwise, I did not really have many challenges. The biggest challenge was probably leaving Paris when the semester ended 😊

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
